deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the construction, begun on the previous page, of the Hilbert tensor product. The setting is two Hilbert spaces E and F. The algebraic tensor product E⊗F carries the sesquilinear form defined on elementary tensors by (5): (x1⊗y1, x2⊗y2) = (x1,x2)(y1,y2). The previous page showed this form is positive definite. It did so by restricting to E0⊗F0 with E0, F0 finite-dimensional and using orthonormal bases, which gives formula (6).

This page begins with the definition. E⊗F, with this pre-Hilbert structure and the norm ||u||_2, is completed to give E ⊗̂_2 F, which is a Hilbert space.

Next comes a Proposition. If (e_i) is an orthonormal basis (Hilbert basis) of E and (f_j) one of F, then (e_i⊗f_j) is an orthonormal basis of E ⊗̂_2 F. The proof has two steps.
- Orthonormality follows from (6).
- Totality: let E0 and F0 be the algebraic spans of the e_i and of the f_j. They are dense in E and F. Hence E0⊗F0, which is the span of the e_i⊗f_j, is dense in E⊗F for the 2-norm, and therefore dense in the completion.

Two formulas are then recorded: (7) ||x⊗y||_2 = ||x|| ||y||, equivalently (x⊗y, x⊗y) = (x,x)(y,y).

Finally, the canonical isomorphism between the conjugate of E⊗F and Ē⊗F̄ (formula (1), from an earlier page) respects the pre-Hilbert structures. Passing to completions gives (8): the conjugate of E ⊗̂_2 F is canonically Ē ⊗̂_2 F̄.

The purpose is to set up the Hilbert tensor product as a model case within Grothendieck's 1953 theory of topological tensor products. The next page identifies L^2(μ) ⊗̂_2 E with L^2_E(μ).
errors: Minor ordering gap: density of E0⊗F0 in E⊗F for the 2-norm needs continuity of (x,y) ↦ x⊗y. That continuity follows from formula (7), which is only stated afterwards. The argument is correct once (7) is used.
The cross-reference 'd'après (4)' for orthonormality almost certainly should be '(6)', the Kronecker formula on the previous page.

ideas.what: Hilbert tensor product, defined as the completion of the algebraic tensor product under the inner product (x1⊗y1, x2⊗y2) = (x1,x2)(y1,y2)
ideas.where_published: Produits tensoriels topologiques et espaces nucléaires (Memoirs AMS 16, 1955), where Hilbert–Schmidt tensor products are discussed

ideas.what: Tensor products of orthonormal bases form an orthonormal basis of the Hilbert tensor product
ideas.modern_name: orthonormal basis of a tensor product

ideas.what: Conjugate of the Hilbert tensor product is canonically Ē ⊗̂_2 F̄
ideas.modern_name: compatibility of complex conjugation with tensor products

deep.surprise_reason: Standard textbook construction of the Hilbert tensor product with routine verifications. Nothing new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: First line likely reads: 'Espace E⊗F, muni de la structure préhilbertienne définie par (5)'. The '(3)' is probably '(5)'. The norm is denoted ||u||_2.
'Rapp!' should be 'Prop.' (underlined: Proposition), followed by 'Soient E et F deux espaces de Hilbert.'
'd'après (4)' is probably '(6)' in the original sense, though the image may read '(4)'.
Text in the proof: 'les e_i ⊗ f_j engendrent un sous-espace dense dans E ⊗̂_2 F', with '(si E0 (resp. F0) désignent les sous-espaces engendrés par les e_i (resp. les f_j))'.
Formula (8): the overline is over E ⊗̂_2 F (written ⊗ with superscript (2)), and the right side is Ē ⊗̂_2 F̄. The second ⊗ symbol carries a similar superscript mark.
